A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fixed-regret and fixed-reward bandit framework. Their main text, equations, figures, proofs, and experimental appendices support comparison; v1 Appendix E corresponds to v2 Appendix F.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original simulations comparing cumulative regret across algorithms, horizons, abstention costs, and synthetic bandit instances.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain these original simulation results, including averages over 2,000 independent trials.

M1.justification: The two main algorithms are unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds an adaptation for arm-specific abstention costs, modifying the lower confidence bounds and abstention thresholds and using the maximum cost for the gap-independent trigger.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian synthetic instances with K=7 and K=10, plus fixed-regret random instances with K=20 and K=30. Heterogeneous costs and online advertising are added as theory or motivation, without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Fixed-regret comparisons retain Less-Exploring TS. Fixed-reward comparisons retain Less-Exploring TS and KL-UCB++, alongside the same FRW-TSwA and FRW-UCBwA realizations. Both non-abstaining baselines are plotted in Figures 4–5 in both versions.

E3.justification: The simulation protocols remain unchanged, including horizon sweeps, fixed T=10,000 cost sweeps, c=0.1 for fixed-regret horizon comparisons, and c=0.9 for fixed-reward horizon comparisons. No new empirical protocol accompanies the theoretical extensions.

E4.justification: The abstention-cost sensitivity analyses and random-instance checks in Figures 3 and 5–7 already appear in v1. No ablation, robustness experiment, or empirical case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 2,000 independent trials and standard deviations as error bars. No change to run counts, seed reporting, or statistical procedures is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 2–7 retain the same regret curves, comparator rankings, and horizon- and cost-dependent findings. The fixed-reward and random-instance results move from Appendix E to F without new or revised empirical outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a heterogeneous-cost regret definition, matching upper and lower bounds in Theorems 6–7, and an abbreviated proof adaptation, broadening the formal setting beyond a common cost. Appendix B also adds an asymptotic comparison with a deterministic extra arm. The original main theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central novelty and simultaneous asymptotic/minimax optimality claims are retained. The conclusion additionally asserts constant-time overhead beyond arm selection and extends the claimed applicability beyond Gaussian rewards, subject to handling boundary cases.

C2.justification: v2 explains why observation-preserving abstention differs from adding a deterministic arm, discusses applicability to stochastic abstention costs with known expectation, and explicitly limits the clinical-trial example to stylized motivation. Existing empirical interpretations and linear-bandit limitations remain.

D1.justification: Simulation-generation recipes, pseudocode for the evaluated algorithms, and the disclosure that KL-UCB++ requires the horizon are retained. No code access, hardware specifications, measured runtimes, or additional experimental implementation details are supplied.

R1.justification: Remark 2 adds Alon et al. (2017) and Liu et al. (2018) to discuss graph-feedback bandits. Appendix B further positions the framework against an extra deterministic-arm reduction. The existing related-work coverage is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author presentation, edits the abstract and selected explanations, adds acknowledgments, and integrates the former Remark 3.2 into Section 3. The new Appendix B and subsection D.3 expand the document, while the main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantially revised typography, author layout, and algorithm and equation displays. The same seven figures are resized and repositioned; Figures 2 and 3 change from adjacent column displays to vertically stacked displays.

improvement.justification: The extra-arm comparison, clearer explanations of the abstention criteria, and explicit qualification of the clinical motivation improve understanding of the original work. The heterogeneous-cost extension broadens scope, although its abbreviated proof and ambiguous cost index in Equation (18) limit that gain. With the principal guarantees and empirical evidence retained, the clearest overall improvement is modest clarification.
